en: You're not coming with us?
If we don't stay, there won't be anyone to tell the others of your incredibly daring escape.
Besides, I hate the cold. Normally you couldn't pay me to go out in this. It's only worth it if I'm rescuing some friends.
Himura-san...
You guys need to take care, okay? It's dangerous out there. Real dangerous.
They say a man-eating bear lumbers around these parts. It's supposed to be two meters tall!
Oh, for... Is this really the time for your tall tales?
Oh, but it's true! I swear it on... Ah, whatever. Get outta here, you two!
I owe you a deep debt.
Sure. When I get out you can buy me dinner.
I'll treat ya to the tastiest tripe BBQ ya ever had. You'll be eatin' till ya burst.
Haha, why not short ribs? Why not, uh, <Italic>anything</Italic> but tripe?
Baba-chan, what ya said earlier... is it true? Ya really belong to the Kitakata Family? The one that offed Majima?
Yes, it's true. But Kosaka-san, I swear I got nothing to do with any killings outside. I can't help what family I'm from.
I know that. What I'm concerned about is your safety.
Huh? What is this about?
It's a feeling I have. Everything about this whole chain of events feels planned out... carefully scripted...
Kugihara and his gang transfer here six months ago, and immediately start assaulting Saejima.
Clearly, their objective was to extend your sentence.
And then, you were expelled from your clan.
I began processing your parole, and Kugihara tried another tactic. He set Baba up so that Saejima's request would be denied.
Why is he trying so hard to extend your incarceration?
Could it be to prevent Saejima-aniki from getting revenge for Majima?
That's possible.
Perhaps Kugihara knew about the hit before it happened.
Perhaps he was sent here with the express purpose of ensuring Saejima's continued confinement.
I mean, the Kitakata Family certainly has influence.
But I just don't see them being able to pull strings at the Ministry of Justice like that.
Well-reasoned. There are only two organizations powerful enough to influence the Ministry of Justice.
One is Kansai's Omi Alliance. And the other one is...
The Tojo Clan. Kugihara's got ties to my... old family. Is that what you're sayin'?
Yes. Given the scale of their behavior, that seems to be the most logical hypothesis.
No way! I don't believe it.
Why would the Tojo do that to one of their own people?
There's a traitor inside the clan. That's the explanation.
But why turn traitor?
When Saejima came here, he was slated to be Tojo's next captain.
Seriously!? Saejima-aniki?
This traitor might have wanted to neutralize Saejima and any power he holds within the clan.
So that's why they expelled him...
Right, but they couldn't just expel him without doing anything else, since doing so actually improves his chances of early parole.
So they pressured the Ministry of Justice to reject Saejima's parole application.
Thus, they keep the powerful Taiga Saejima trapped and languishing in Abashiri. That's how I read it.
In the back of the exercise yard, outside the southwest gate, there's a parked snowmobile. This is the key.
I'm letting you break out of here.
The warden is dead. Murder. We don't know who did it; an investigation is underway.
Geez... what happened?
He was traveling to Tokyo to inquire as to why Saejima's parole was denied.
The assailants attacked him as he got out of his taxi at Sapporo Airport.
And that's not all. This afternoon, we will be receiving almost a hundred new inmates⑬transfers from other institutions.
There's never been such an enormous influx before, and no explanation was given.
I'm afraid they've been sent with a specific purpose in mind.
For real? You think those guys are coming to kill Saejima-aniki?
Matters have become much bigger than any of us could have imagined.
If nothing is done, your blood will be on my hands, Saejima. Yours too, Baba, now that you are involved.
I won't allow that to happen. I am sworn to defend the rights of all citizens.
But if ya let us go, your superiors will have ya strung up by your ankles.
I'm prepared to face the consequences of my decision.
With no regrets, I will be tendering my resignation. Integrity is more important than any job.
Kosaka-han...
Saejima-san. Baba-san. You are officially no longer incarcerated at this facility.
You have each sufficiently atoned for your offenses. Your freedom of movement is restored. I will impart just one request...
Show the world who the real enemy is⑬those responsible for the warden's murder.
Later tonight, after your cellmates are asleep, leave your cell.
A guard will leave your cell door unlocked.
Exit the building, cut across the grounds, and go out the southwest gate.
The late hour should hide you from the eyes of Kugihara and any other adversaries.
We'll do it.
One last thing. Please promise me this...
If, on the outside, you ever find the true culprit, don't kill him.
Report him to authorities. Send him to prison alive.
At that point, it will be our job to carry out justice.
I promise.
Deputy Warden... So it's you who asked for us.
I enjoyed the fake reason for it, too. What's this really about?
Forgive me for meeting you out here. I wished to protect us from any potential eavesdroppers near my office.
What's going on? Kinda freaking out here.
Saejima's application for parole was denied.
Huh? No way, why?
These applications are evaluated by our Regional Parole Board. At least, that's the normal procedure.
This time, however, the Ministry of Justice appears to be involved. The rejection came directly from them.
Whoa, that's weird. Isn't it...?
Saejima is a major yakuza figure. Naturally he's on the radar of many police organizations.
Perhaps his status is the only reason the Ministry has taken an interest. That is what I hope. But I have my doubts.
Well, is that all?
"Is that all"?
I told ya already. I don't intend to apply for parole.
Also, Baba-chan ain't got nothin' to do with this.
Me, there's only one thing I wanna know.
It's about Goro Majima, isn't it?
The guy in the newspaper? I was wondering why you were so shook up.
Majima is the patriarch of the Tojo Clan's Majima Family and lieutenant advisor to the overall clan.
The Majima Family is several thousand strong. It's the largest faction within the clan. And its boss just so happens to be Saejima's sworn brother.
He was a close friend of yours, Saejima-aniki? I'm sorry for your loss.
From what we understand, the person behind the murder is Taizo Kitakata, the patriarch of Sapporo's Kitakata Family.
Kitakata?
Majima was attempting to arrange the acquisition of the Kitakata. He was conducting the deal in Sapporo, ordered there by Tojo's chairman.
During his meeting with Patriarch Kitakata, he was shot and killed.
Baba, surely now you know why you're here?
What's he talking about, Baba-chan?
The Kitakata Family... That's who I used to run with.
We should discuss this elsewhere. Wait for me in the storeroom. I won't be long.
We need to avoid being seen together.
Why are ya trustin' us not to pull anything?
I don't trust you... but I do trust you'll want to hear the rest of what I'm going to say.
Um, Aniki...
We can talk later. For now, let's just go hear the deputy warden out. Okay?
We owe ya so much. If not for you, Baba and I'd both be bear food by now.
Really, thank you very much!
I'm sure Okudera-san would've wanted to see you off properly, too.
Yeah. There're still a few things I wanna ask him, so I might be back sometime.
Oh, yeah. Okudera-san had a message for you two.
He said not to forget this one thing⑬
"Killing is only justified when it is for hunting or protecting one's own life."
That's it. He wanted me to pass that on when it was time for you to leave the mountain.
Got it. I won't forget.
Let's get going now, Aniki.
You take care, then.
You okay movin' around already?
Yes, I can manage.
I'm sorry, Aniki. I'm just dead weight for you now.
Never mind me. Ya gotta thank the guy that saved ya, first.
Huh? Who is that?
His name's Okudera-han. He's an old hunter. This is a hunting village up in the mountains.
No kidding?
You ain't outta the woods yet. Quit talkin' and rest up some more.
Okay... I'm sorry about all this.
Just hold tight. I'm gonna go out an' tell Okudera-han ya woke up.
(Better go find Okudera-han.)
(I've been here a while, but Okudera-han still ain't back.)
(The sun's set, too. I'm gettin' worried. Hope he's safe and sound.)
Okudera-han! You're all right!
Yeah, more or less.
He was out there longer, so he's worse off than you.
But if he takes it easy, he should be fine. Let him rest up a while.
What happened with that bear? Did ya bring it down?
Nope. The snow storm got worse. If I kept after it, I wouldn't have made it back.
The villagers seem to think ya got some special connection to that Yama-oroshi.
Word is ya dedicated yer life to hunting it down. Why's that?
Hunting is all about man's survival instincts. We hunt to live.
For thousands of years, we've fed on the meat of animals we've killed.
The meat in this stew is from an animal I hunted, too.
We kill to eat, so it's our duty to finish every last bite. That's what hunting is about.
But I don't want to hunt that bear.
Whaddya want to do, then?
I just want to slay the thing. I'm going after that bear to murder it.
We humans are funny things.
We kill people out of hatred so easily. Even if our lives aren't on the line.
That's why it's a crime, and why you pay for it by going to prison.
But only a few people come out of prison repenting for the fact they've killed another human being.
Most insist they did what they did because they had no choice.
Any killing not done to eat or protect yourself is purely on your head.
No matter what excuse a murderer may give, they're just fooling themselves.
Ya lecturin' me now?
Or are ya talkin' about your own past? Which is it?
Neither. I'm reflecting on my own personal reasons for going after that bear.
Because essentially, my only reason for even being here is to murder it.
Enough talk. We killed these animals. We should do right by them and eat all of the meat.
So ya saved my ass, out there in the wilderness.
You should sit still. You've got bad frostbite; moving around will damage the tissue surrounding the frozen parts.
Just try to relax.
Ya see another guy out there? I was travelin' with a friend.
He could still be out there. I gotta go find 'im!
Didn't you hear what I said? Moving will kill you.
I can't just sit here when my buddy could be in trouble.
And <Italic>I</Italic> can't sit here and watch you leave!
If you go up into the mountains untrained, you'll end up stranded. You think I need that on my conscience?
I'll go find this friend of yours.
Ya willin' to do that? For a couple o' guys you don't know?
Once a bear gets a taste for human flesh, there'll be trouble.
The beast might come down to the village for more of its new favorite food.
The bear that attacked you⑬it was twice as big as normal. Am I right?
Yeah, thereabouts. Ya sayin' it's some kinda man-eater?
Don't know...
It's just rumors. Rumors from a long time ago.
The point is, if I don't save your friend he could end up as bear food. And then that's just another problem for me.
(...Hang in there, Baba-chan.)
Take a stroll outside if you want.
But if you insist on getting yourself killed, please do it where you won't be eaten by a bear.
There's a change of clothes there. They're old rags of mine, but you're welcome to use them.
I never thanked ya for savin' me.
I'm Saejima, and I owe ya my life. Thank you.
My name's Okudera. Goodbye.
(I can't just sit here... I can check the place out, at least.)
You now have access to a hideout.
Here you can save your game, move items to the Item Box, and view your play stats.
Furthermore, your health will recover while at a hideout.
Baba-chan? Okudera-han!
Why did you come here!?
Baba needs help. I can't put all of that on you.
...You're hurt, too.
Did Yama-oroshi get ya?
Got careless. I'm getting old.
Forget me. Take care of him.
He's badly hurt, but hanging on. Hurry, let's take him to the village!
Gwwwoooaar!
It smells our blood. ...It's coming.
Agh! Missed!
I'll give chase! You take him back to the village!
But you're hurt, too!
It doesn't matter. Hurry! No time to waste!
